pr_body:
Closes #19420

This is my first code contribution to ORA, so there's probably a lot of room for improvement

The way map refresh works:
`MapCache` has 2 instances of `MapDirectoryTracker` tracking both the custom and official maps folders for changes respectively. When they detect something, they analyse what and if they need to take action, then they put or edit appropriate actions in `mapActionQueue`. Whenever `MapCache` is queried for maps, it is updated from the records in `mapActionQueue`

I needed to queue actions because `FileSystemWatcher` is spamming quite a lot and those actions are often in an illogical order. F.e. when I add a file it calls `Changed`,  then `Created`. Another example is when I add / edit an uncompressed map, then it spams a ton of actions. Furthermore maps are never deleted from `MapCache`. So if we were to update `MapCache` at every `FileSystemWatcher` event it would likely clog up memory with very similar maps. The queue is designed to address all of this by updating `MapCache` only when it is required

Map editor no longer updates the cache, since it already happens when when MapDirectoryTracker kicks in

The game now selects the last edited map when entering map chooser. If in lobby the selected map is updated it, it will switch to the updated version. I'm not sure if this change is necessary, but it would be fairly convenient.
pr_comments: Fixed all bugs and crashes I could find. I changed ComputeUID to include map.png. ~~This change should be done in another pr, but I added it here temporarily as it is a very noticeable bug~~ #19891

Now when a user picks a map in map chooser that has been updated while user was in map chooser window, the game will act as if nothing was selected and exit. 

I also separated `MapDirectoryTracker` class into it's own file and rebased

Now when you force start or click on a ready checkbox, the game properly handles the selected map becoming unavailable. The previous behaviour was quite unpolished. On game start the screen become black, and then the lobby is refreshed.
Handled a crash. Now if you try to play a map in `MissionSelector` that has been marked as unavailable you will exit `MissionSelector`. Same behaviour as Map Editor `MapChooser`

> Now when you force start or click on a ready checkbox

I undid the checkbox behaviour (but kept force start). My solution felt a bit hacky and honestly unnecessary. It's a minor polish feature that can be added in a followup pr

rebased and changed console reporting from "Added 'map'" to "'map' was added"

I'm unsure wether we should keep this reporting. For me it made sense to exist, however when looking back on it, you wouldn't really use it for anything
I am fine with it, as the map editor also reports file system changes that way.

issue_context.title: Ability to test the map without restarting the game.
issue_context.body:
Why does the open-ra load all the resources in bulk? Moreover, when you start the game and then when you start the level.

It is very inconvenient to test any missions. I would like to do solo missions. Studied lua. But I like cameo mods, and I just can't do it. It takes too long.

Suggested solution: missions need to be updated, possibly with some kind of note in the config "in development, dynamic update".
I cannot constantly restart the game to test the map. It just kills any motivation, because I won't get paid for it.
comments: I don't understand this issue. You can make changes in a map and restart a mission without restarting the client.

> I don't understand this issue. You can make changes in a map and restart a mission without restarting the client.

I think what he means is that if you mod a .yaml file for a map you have to reload the game for it to take effect

> I think what he means is that if you mod a .yaml file for a map you have to reload the game for it to take effect

I think you can. I know for sure you can change a .lua without restarting the game client.

A intermediate solution perhaps could be that you can start a map/game from the command line. Similar to how you can start the game with a replay. This would skip the main menu and just start in game. Would avoid loading the shell map.

Reloading the resources of a map - restarting a map - is possible. Reloading the yaml files that are part of a mod is likely not something that can be done dynamically easily or very fast - as it would require a full reload of all yaml files, the whole internal game state. Marking yaml files as dynamic/in-development/reloadable is not an easy solution to implement - because of the many relations between objects in a mod.

> A intermediate solution perhaps could be that you can start a map/game from the command line. 

This is already possible!
```
./launch-game.sh Game.Mod=ra Launch.Map=a88670ababc446033321595026f7104800c9aa6b
```

will launch directly into allies-01 (using the map hash on bleed, hash might be different on other tags - use `./utility.sh ra --map-hash mods/ra/allies-01` to find it).

Perhaps a nice feature if you could start the game with a Replay and tell it stop replay x ticks before the end - after which the player can take over and continue to play where he/she left off in the past. Or more in general, that you can take over a replay - that has no remote players.

review_comments: Similarly the braces around the `LoadMap` call can go since it's on one line.

Can also remove the next level of outer braces, so:
```c#
foreach (...)
    foreach (...)
        LoadMap(...);
```

Because `FileSystemWatcher ` is `IDisposable`, we need to ensure that logic is plumbed through, so we don't have file watchers living forever once we stop caring about them.

- Change the class to `public sealed class MapDirectoryTracker : IDisposable`
- Implement `public void Dispose` with a body of `watcher.Dispose();`
- In `MapCache`, update the `Dispose` method to also loop over and dispose every tracker.

The delete button was querying `mapCache` every frame, defeating the whole purpose of the queue. 

All it wanted to know is if the map chooser tab was changed. As as `currentTab` is already updated on a switch, there's no need to query `mapChache`

If I'm following the logic here now, we're preselecting the map you've just changed on disk for your convenience? That seems handy.

I think a comment like `// Check for updated maps, if the user has edited a map we'll preselect it for them.` would be more descriptive as it's giving a 'why' instead of a 'what'.
I'll change the comment right away
This can be private, we don't use an access keyword for methods using the default access so just `void UpdateMaps()` is fine.
